correctness.rationale: The unit cut has exact tail \(x^{-2}\). Every non-unit separator has exponent at least \(2+\min(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)\), so the block tail is asymptotic to \(\mu_Px^{-2}\). Subtracting \(vP_i\) preserves that tail because pivot gaps are exponentially bounded. Its truncated second moment is asymptotic to \(2\mu_P\log x\), yielding the normal-domain-of-attraction scale \(\sqrt{n\log n}\); the pivot residual is tight and negligible.
